and incapable of going to a village, a city, or a town; even so, Kauśika, generosity, ethical discipline, patience, vigor, and meditative concentration receive the name "perfection" only through the Perfection of Wisdom.
Without the perfection of wisdom, one becomes like one born blind because of the lack of a guide;
being incapable of entering the path to omniscience,
how indeed could one attain omniscience?
Furthermore, Kauśika, when giving, morality, patience, vigor, and meditative concentration are embraced by the perfection of wisdom,
then they receive the designation and the name of "perfections.
For at that time, these five perfections obtain their eyes for entering the path to omniscience and for the attainment of omniscience.
Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva bring forth the perfection of wisdom?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Śāriputra: "Śāriputra, the bringing forth of form should be seen;
likewise for feeling, perception, and mental formations."
Śāriputra, the production of consciousness is to be seen as follows:
Śāriputra, that which is the production of the five aggregates is called, Śāriputra, the production of the perfection of wisdom.
Through such an accomplishment, the accomplishment of the five aggregates is called the accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom; this is what is meant by "accomplishment."

When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, by such an accomplishment, what dharma does the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) that has been accomplished establish?
The Blessed One replied: "Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom accomplished in this way does not establish any dharma whatsoever.
Śāriputra, when it does not establish any dharma whatsoever,"
then it receives the designation "perfection of wisdom."
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, does this perfection of wisdom not even bestow omniscience?
The Blessed One replied: "Kauśika, as for what you say—that 'does this perfection of wisdom not even bestow omniscience?'—it does not bestow it in the manner of apprehension."
"It does not dedicate in accordance with the name, nor does it dedicate in accordance with the formative activity.
Śakra asked: "In what way, then, O Blessed One, does it dedicate?"
The Blessed One said: "Kauśika, it is in such a way that he entrusts it, that he does not entrust it.
Śakra said: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how far this perfection of wisdom goes; it does not produce any dharma whatsoever, nor does it cause any dharma whatsoever to cease."
The perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of the non-arising and non-cessation of all phenomena; it is neither present nor absent.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should even perceive in this way, he will distance himself from this perfection of wisdom;
he will make this perfection of wisdom empty."
"He will render this perfection of wisdom empty;
he will not make this perfection of wisdom real.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: "So it is, Subhūti, so it is."
There is, Subhūti,
a way in which they will distance themselves from this perfection of wisdom, and a way in which they will make this perfection of wisdom empty.
He will treat this perfection of wisdom as empty;
he will not make this perfection of wisdom his own.
For what reason?
For when the perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, is elucidated, form is not elucidated;
nor is feeling, nor perception, nor mental formations;
nor is consciousness elucidated.
The fruit of stream-entry is not elucidated;
the fruit of once-returning is not elucidated;
the fruit of non-returning is not elucidated.
Neither the state of arhatship is fully elucidated,
nor is the state of a pratyekabuddha fully elucidated, nor is the state of a buddha fully elucidated.
The Elder Subhūti said: "O Bhagavat, this is a great perfection, namely, the perfection of wisdom.
The Bhagavat said: "What do you think, Subhūti? By what reasoning is this a great perfection, namely, the perfection of wisdom?
The Elder Subhūti said: "O Bhagavat, it does not make form great, nor does it make it small."
It does not contract form, nor does it expand it;
likewise, it does not [contract or expand] feeling, perception, or mental formations.
O Blessed One, it does not make consciousness great, nor does it make it small.
It does not contract consciousness nor does it disperse it;
even those powers of a Tathāgata, the powers of a Tathāgata, it neither strengthens nor weakens them.
He neither contracts nor disperses;
even that omniscience,
he neither magnifies nor diminishes.
He neither contracts nor distracts [the mind].
Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, omniscience is indeed neither contracted nor distracted.
If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva perceives even in this way,
he does not course in the perfection of wisdom.
How much less so could one who perceives thus: "In this way, endowed with the knowledge of the All-Knowing One, I shall teach the Dharma to sentient beings;
in this way, I shall lead these sentient beings to final nirvāṇa"?
For what reason?
For this apprehension of a "sentient being"—the thought, "I shall bring these sentient beings to final nirvana"—is not the outflow of the perfection of wisdom;
rather, it would be a great non-apprehension for him.
Why is that?
For the perfection of wisdom should be understood as having the nature of the non-substantiality of sentient beings;
by virtue of the non-substantiality of sentient beings, the non-substantiality of the perfection of wisdom should be understood;
by virtue of the solitude of sentient beings, the solitude of the perfection of wisdom should be understood.

Through the inconceivability of sentient beings, the inconceivability of the perfection of wisdom should be known; through the non-perishing nature of sentient beings, the non-perishing nature of the perfection of wisdom should be known;
through the lack of full awakening regarding sentient beings, the lack of full awakening regarding the perfection of wisdom should be known.

Through the non-realization of the true nature of sentient beings, one should understand the non-realization of the true nature of the perfection of wisdom. Through the attainment of the power of sentient beings, one should understand the attainment of the power of the Tathāgata.
By this method, O Blessed One, this is the great perfection, namely, the perfection of wisdom.

Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, from where has that bodhisattva mahāsattva come who, having passed away there, has been reborn here, and who will have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom, and will not doubt, will not be perplexed, and will not be hesitant?"

"Blessed One, for how long has that bodhisattva mahāsattva practiced, such that he will follow, awaken to, and cause others to awaken to this perfection of wisdom according to its meaning, its nature, its method of meaning, and its method of dharma?
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra: "Śāriputra, that bodhisattva mahāsattva..."
It should be known that he has passed away from other world-systems, having attended upon and questioned the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and has now been reborn here.
Why is that?
Śāriputra, any bodhisattva mahāsattva who has passed away from other world-systems, having attended upon and questioned the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—
Having been reborn here, he should hear this profound perfection of wisdom being spoken, taught, instructed, and expounded;
and having heard this perfection of wisdom, he should conceive the notion of the Teacher toward this perfection of wisdom, thinking: "The Teacher has appeared before me."
He gives rise to the thought, "I have seen the Teacher.
While the Perfection of Wisdom is being spoken, taught, instructed, and expounded, he lends an ear and listens with reverence.
He does not interrupt the discourse;
Śāriputra, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva should be known as one who has practiced for a long time;
Śāriputra, such a bodhisattva mahāsattva should be known as one who has attended upon many Buddhas.

Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "But, Blessed One, is it possible to hear the perfection of wisdom, or to perceive it, or to attend to it, or to produce it, or to comprehend it?
Is this that perfection of wisdom?"
Can this perfection of wisdom be pointed out or heard as being "here" or "there," or by means of such a form, characteristic, or sign?
The Blessed One said: "Not so, Subhūti.

This perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, cannot be pointed out, nor heard, nor perceived, nor reflected upon, nor produced, nor maintained, whether by way of the aggregates, the elements, or the sense-fields."
For what reason?
Subhūti, because all dharmas are secluded;
Subhūti, because all dharmas are absolutely secluded, it is impossible to explain, hear, perceive, attend to, produce, or comprehend the perfection of wisdom.
Or rather,
the perfection of wisdom is not to be realized apart from the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields.
Why is that?
Subhūti, the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases themselves are indeed empty, secluded, and peaceful.
Thus, the perfection of wisdom and the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are non-dual and not divided, because they are empty and secluded;
likewise, because they are peaceful, they are not apprehended.
That which is the non-apprehension of all phenomena is called the perfection of wisdom;
when there is no perception, no designation, no conceptualization, and no conventional usage, [that is it].
then it is called the perfection of wisdom.
The Elder Subhūti said: "Blessed One, for how long has that bodhisattva mahāsattva practiced so that he should be known as one who will apply himself to yoga in this profound perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, this must be explained by making a distinction according to the superior faculties of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there may be a way in which bodhisattvas [have practiced under] many hundreds of Buddhas, many..."
Having seen many thousands of Buddhas and hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, and having practiced the holy life (brahmacarya) in their presence,
they would not have faith in this Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), nor would they resolve upon it.
Why is that?

Previously, too, when this profound perfection of wisdom was being spoken, taught, and explained in the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they lacked respect; through their lack of respect, they lacked the desire to listen; and through their lack of desire to listen, they did not attend upon them.
Because they did not attend upon him, they did not inquire; because they did not inquire, they lacked faith;
and because they lacked faith, they departed from those assemblies.

On account of that, by means of the karma they have performed, accumulated, gathered, and piled up— which leads to the ruin of the Dharma— even now, when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being spoken, taught, and explained, they depart from it.
Out of lack of respect, lacking faith, and without conviction, they do not provide their bodies or minds with the necessary cooperation.
Because they do not provide the necessary conditions, they do not know, do not see, do not awaken to, and do not experience this perfection of wisdom;
thus they do not have faith in the perfection of wisdom,
and lacking faith, they do not hear it.
Not hearing, they do not know;
not knowing, they do not see;
not seeing, they do not awaken.
Unaware, they perform, accumulate, gather, and amass actions that lead to the ruin of the Dharma.
By means of those actions leading to the ruin of the Dharma— which have been performed, accumulated, gathered, and amassed— they will further bring about actions that lead to a lack of wisdom.
Because of that karma which has been performed, accumulated, gathered, and heaped up, conducive to poor wisdom, they will reject, repudiate,
and revile this Perfection of Wisdom as it is being spoken, taught, and explained; and having repudiated it, they will depart.
Furthermore, Subhūti, by rejecting, repudiating, and reviling this perfection of wisdom, one rejects and repudiates the omniscience of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present.
It becomes contemptible;
having destroyed their own continuums and being consumed by fire, they [act] toward other persons who possess little intelligence, little wisdom, little merit, and few roots of virtue,
who are endowed with mere faith, mere affection, and mere clarity of mind.

They will discourage, alienate, and turn away even that mere faith, mere affection, mere clarity, and mere aspiration belonging to those beginners who possess only such [qualities] and are incapable [of success],
saying, "One should not train in this."
They will speak these words: "This is not the word of the Buddha.
Thus, having harmed their own mental continuums by causing dissension, and having also harmed the mental continuums of others by causing dissension, they will slander the perfection of wisdom.
When the perfection of wisdom is slandered, omniscience is slandered.
When omniscience is slandered, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present, are slandered;
they will have departed from the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
and they will be estranged from the Dharma.
They will be excluded from the Saṅgha;
thus, in every way and in all respects, they will be entirely excluded from the Three Jewels.
By acting to sever the welfare and happiness of sentient beings, they will accumulate karma that leads to the maturation of the great hells.

By means of such a formation of karma— established and originated by this [action] which leads to the ruin of the Dharma and leads to lack of wisdom— they [will remain] for many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, many hundreds of thousands of years,
many hundreds of millions of years, many billions of years, many hundreds of billions of years, many...
For hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of years they will be reborn in the great hells;
they will pass from one great hell to another great hell.
As they thus pass from one great hell to another for such a very long time, the destruction by fire will manifest.
When the fire-destruction of the world has appeared, they will be cast into the great hells that exist in other world-systems;
they will be reborn in those great hells.

Scattered there, having been reborn in those great hells, they will pass from one great hell to another great hell. As they are thus passing from one great hell to another, the fire that destroys the world will once again manifest there in the same manner. When that fire which destroys the world has manifested, they will pass away from there and be cast once more into the great hells in other world-systems.
They will be reborn in those great hells;
there too, they will likewise pass from one great hell to another great hell.
As they continue for a very long time passing from one great hell to another, even there the fire that destroys the world will manifest in the same manner.

When that conflagration of fire has appeared, they will fall from there once again; by that very same karma which is not yet exhausted and still has a remainder, they will be cast back into this very world-system.
Having been cast there, they will be reborn in the great hells.
There, in those great hells, they will once more experience the immense sufferings of the great hells.
They will experience [the results] for as long as it takes until the destruction by fire occurs once again.
In this way, they will experience karma that results in much suffering.
For what reason?
Precisely because of their ill-spoken words.

Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, even the five deeds of immediate retribution, when committed and accumulated, do not even approximate, nor correspond to, nor resemble this misconduct of mind and this misconduct of speech."
The Blessed One said: "It is so, Śāriputra; it is so.

Śāriputra, the five deeds of immediate retribution, though committed and accumulated, are not even a likeness, nor a correspondence, nor a resemblance to this mental misconduct and verbal misconduct that has been performed."
Of that which has been gathered, accumulated, and heaped up—
whosoever shall think that this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, while it is being spoken, taught, explained, and pointed out, should be opposed, they shall reject it.
They will revile it,
they will say, "One should not train in this," and they will utter the words, "This was not spoken by the Tathāgata."
Then they will also alienate other beings;
having harmed their own mental continuums, they will harm the mental continuums of others.
Having made their own mental continuums poisonous, they will make the mental continuums of others poisonous.
Having perished themselves, they will cause others to perish as well;
not knowing and not understanding the profound Perfection of Wisdom themselves, they will cause others to grasp it incorrectly, speaking the words, "One should not train in this."
Śāriputra, I do not even permit the sight of persons such as these; how much less their living together with them, how much less gain and honor, and how much less a place [to dwell]?
For what reason?
"Śāriputra, such persons as those should be known as corrupters of the Dharma.
Śāriputra, such persons as those should be known as born of the chaff.
Śāriputra, such persons as those should be known as of black birth, of the breed of black serpents."
Śāriputra, all those who think they should listen to such persons as these will meet with disaster through their wrong course.
And those, Śāriputra, who revile the perfection of wisdom—
"Śāriputra, these persons should be known as corrupters of the Dharma.
Śāriputra said, "Blessed One, the Blessed One has not declared the measure of the physical body of that person who, having been reborn there, has entered the great hell.
The Blessed One said, "Let be, Śāriputra, the measure of the physical body of that person who, having been reborn there, has entered the great hell."
For what reason?
Lest, upon hearing the measurement of the physical body of such a person, hot blood should issue from the mouth,
or one should meet with death.
Or he might encounter severe suffering amounting to death, or a grave affliction,
or he might be consumed by fire,
or the dart of sorrow might pierce him.
He might fall into a great abyss,
or wither away, or become languid;
let him not hear of the measure of that most terrifying physical existence in which these defects exist.
The Blessed One did not grant the Venerable Śāriputra the opportunity [to state] what the measure of that person’s physical body would be.
A second time and even a third time, the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One declare to me the measure of that person’s physical body;

it will serve as a light for future generations, so that they may see how, by performing, accumulating, and piling up such verbal and mental karma, one takes on such a vast physical body in the great hells.”

The Blessed One said: "Śāriputra, this very person will provide light for future generations by the fact that he will experience such long-lasting suffering as a result of this unwholesome karma—this mental and vocal misconduct—which was performed, accumulated, gathered, amassed, and piled up.
Śāriputra, it is precisely because of this suffering that its immeasurability and its great magnitude [are made known]."
This very explanation will cause a sense of spiritual urgency (*saṃvega*) to arise in a son or daughter of good family who possesses virtuous qualities.
Thereupon, having desisted from those actions that lead to the ruin of the Dharma, they will perform only the accumulation of merit;
even for the sake of their life, they will not reject the true Dharma, thinking: "May we not encounter such sufferings as these."
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, a son of good family or a daughter of good family must be well-restrained in their actions of body, speech, and mind.
Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, such a great mass of demerit is produced by a mere ill-spoken word as this."
"By what action, Blessed One, is such a great mass of merit produced?
The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, by such ill-spoken words as these, such a great mass of merit is produced.
Subhūti, right here in this well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya, those deluded men will go forth as renunciants."
Those who think that this profound perfection of wisdom should be reviled, think it should be rejected, and think it should be opposed— [they are acting thus].
When the perfection of wisdom is rejected, the awakening of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, is rejected.
When the awakening of the Buddhas is rejected, the omniscience of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, is rejected.
When omniscience is rejected, the True Dharma is rejected.
When the true Dharma is obstructed, the Saṅgha of the Tathāgata’s disciples is obstructed.

When the Saṅgha of the Tathāgata’s disciples is also obstructed, he becomes entirely and in every way excluded from the Three Jewels, and he takes upon himself a great accumulation of unwholesome karma that is even more immeasurable and incalculable.

When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the reason, that such a son of good family or daughter of good family [rejects] this perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One has said: 'Subhūti, that son of good family or daughter of good family will be possessed by Māra;
or else, due to karma conducive to lack of wisdom, he has no faith in these profound dharmas.'"
He lacks faith.
Subhūti, endowed with these two unwholesome qualities, that son of good family or daughter of good family will reject this perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti, that son of good family or daughter of good family will have fallen into the hands of evil friends.
He will either be lacking in application, or he will be attached to the aggregates,
or he will be one who exalts himself, disparages others, and looks for their faults.

Subhūti, by these four characteristics as well, that son of good family or daughter of good family will be possessed [of such qualities] who considers this Perfection of Wisdom— as it is being spoken, taught, and explained— to be something to be rejected.
The seventh chapter, titled "Hell," in the Noble Eight Thousand Line Perfection of Wisdom.
(Vaidya 93) Chapter Eight: Purity.

Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to resolve upon by one who is not diligent, who is devoid of roots of merit, and who has fallen into the hands of evil friends."
The Blessed One said: "So it is, Subhūti; so it is.

Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to resolve with faith by one who is not diligent, whose roots of merit are meager, who is dull-witted, who lacks aspiration, who has heard little, whose wisdom is inferior, who is supported by evil friends, and who is of a nature that does not wish to hear or inquire about wholesome qualities."
By one who is not devoted to the teachings.
Subhūti said: "How indeed, Blessed One, is this perfection of wisdom so profound that it is difficult to resolve upon?
The Blessed One replied: "Form, Subhūti, is neither bound nor liberated. For what reason?"
Subhūti, because form lacks intrinsic nature, form is neither bound nor liberated.
Likewise, feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness, Subhūti, are neither bound nor liberated.
For what reason?
Subhūti, because consciousness lacks intrinsic nature, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.
Subhūti, the prior limit of form is neither bound nor liberated.
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, form has no intrinsic nature in the past;
and, Subhūti, the future limit of form is neither bound nor liberated.
For what reason?
Subhūti, form has the nature of being without limit in the future;
Subhūti, present form is neither bound nor liberated.
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, present form has no intrinsic nature;
likewise for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
Subhūti, the prior limit of consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, consciousness has no intrinsic nature in its prior limit.
Subhūti, the future limit of consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, consciousness has the nature of no-own-being in its future limit.
Subhūti, present consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, present consciousness has no intrinsic nature of its own.
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to resolve upon;

O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is extremely difficult to resolve upon for one who is not diligent, who has not planted roots of virtue, who has fallen into the hands of evil friends, who is under the sway of Māra, who is indolent, of inferior energy, whose mindfulness is lost, and who is of poor wisdom."
The Blessed One said: "So it is, Subhūti; so it is.
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to resolve upon;

Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is supremely difficult to resolve upon for one who is not diligent, who has not planted roots of merit, who has fallen into the hands of evil friends, who is under the sway of Māra, who is indolent, of inferior vigor, and whose mindfulness is lost."
By one of poor wisdom.
For what reason?
Subhūti, that which is the purity of form—
That which is the purity of the fruit is the purity of form.
For in this way, Subhūti, the purity of form and the purity of the fruit are non-dual; they are not divided, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
For in this way, Subhūti, from the purity of the fruit comes the purity of form, and from the purity of form comes the purity of the fruit.
It is the same for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
Subhūti, that which is the purity of consciousness is the purity of the fruit;
that which is the purity of the fruit is the purity of consciousness.
For thus, Subhūti, the purity of consciousness and the purity of the fruit are non-dual; they are not divided, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
For thus, Subhūti, from the purity of the fruit comes the purity of consciousness, and from the purity of consciousness comes the purity of the fruit.
Furthermore, Subhūti, that which is the purity of form is the purity of omniscience.
That which is the purity of omniscience is the purity of form.
Thus, Subhūti, the purity of form and the purity of omniscience are non-dual; they are not divided, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
For it is thus, Subhūti: from the purity of omniscience comes the purity of form.
Through the purity of form, there is the purity of omniscience;
likewise for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
Subhūti, that which is the purity of consciousness is the purity of omniscience.
That which is the purity of omniscience is the purity of consciousness.
For thus, Subhūti, the purity of consciousness and the purity of omniscience are non-dual; they are not divided, undifferentiated, and uninterrupted.
For in this way, Subhūti, from the purity of omniscience comes the purity of consciousness,
and from the purity of consciousness comes the purity of omniscience.
Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is profound.
The Blessed One said: "Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is illuminating."
The Blessed One said, "Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said, "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is light.
The Blessed One said, "Because of its purity, Śāriputra."
He said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is without reconnection.
The Blessed One said: "Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is without affliction."
The Blessed One said: "Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is non-attainment and non-realization.
The Blessed One said: "Because of its purity, Śāriputra."
He said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is non-production.
The Blessed One said: "Because of its purity, Śāriputra. He said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is absolutely non-arising within the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm."
The Blessed One said, “Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said, “Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom neither knows nor perceives.
The Blessed One said, “Because of its purity, Śāriputra.”
He asked: "Blessed One, does the perfection of wisdom not know and not perceive?
The Blessed One replied: "Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom does not know and does not perceive form. Why is that?"
Because of its purity, Śāriputra, feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness, Śāriputra, do not know and do not perceive the perfection of wisdom.
For what reason? Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom does not do anything to diminish omniscience."
“Does it not perform a service?
The Blessed One said, “Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
He said, “Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom does not grasp at any dharma whatsoever.”
“Does he not relinquish it?
The Blessed One said, “Because of its purity, Śāriputra.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, is the purity of form due to the purity of the self?”
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti.
Subhūti said: "Blessed One, is the purity of feeling, perception, and mental formations due to the purity of the self?
Blessed One, is the purity of consciousness due to the purity of the self?"
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti.
Subhūti asked: "Blessed One, is the purity of the fruit due to the purity of the self?
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti."
He asked: "Blessed One, is the purity of omniscience due to the purity of the self?
The Blessed One replied: "Subhūti, it is because of its absolute purity.
He asked: "Blessed One, is there neither attainment nor realization due to the purity of the self?"
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti.
Subhūti asked: "Blessed One, is form limitless because the self is limitless?
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti."
He asked: "Blessed One, is it because the self is limitless that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also limitless?
The Blessed One replied: "Because they are absolutely pure, Subhūti.
He said: "Blessed One, such is the realization of this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Is this his perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said, "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti.
The Venerable Subhūti said, "Furthermore, Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom does not exist on the further shore,"
"It does not stand on the further shore, nor does it stand between the two, being unconditioned.
The Blessed One said: "Because of its absolute purity, Subhūti."

The Venerable Subhūti said: "Even so, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva will perceive [them] in this way; he will abandon this perfection of wisdom and distance himself from this perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Subhūti! It is even so."
Subhūti, it is so.
And why is that?
For even from a name, Subhūti, there is attachment; even from a sign, there is attachment.

When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how far this perfection of wisdom has been well-proclaimed, well-expounded, and well-established, in that even these attachments have been declared by the Blessed One.
Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the venerable Subhūti: "What, venerable Subhūti, are those attachments?"
Subhūti said: "Venerable Śāriputra, to say 'form is empty' is an attachment.
Likewise for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, venerable Śāriputra, to say 'consciousness is empty' is an attachment."
To perceive past phenomena as "past phenomena" is attachment;
to perceive future phenomena as "future phenomena" is attachment;
to perceive present phenomena as "present phenomena" is attachment.
If a person belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle perceives that "by this first production of the thought of awakening, such a mass of merit is generated," that is attachment.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Subhūti: "In what sense, noble Subhūti, is there attachment?

Subhūti replied: "If, Kauśika, one perceives that thought of awakening, thinking, 'This is that first thought of awakening,' and then dedicates it, thinking, 'I dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening'—that is attachment."
Furthermore, that son of good family or daughter of good family who has set out in the Mahāyāna is not able to transform the nature of the mind.
Therefore, Kauśika, when demonstrating, exhorting, inspiring,
and gladdening others toward unexcelled perfect enlightenment, one should demonstrate, exhort, and inspire them by following what is real.
He should gladden them;
in this way, that son of good family or daughter of good family neither harms himself nor causes others to adopt [the practice] through an undertaking authorized by the Buddhas.
And all these millions of attachments of his become abandoned.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the venerable Subhūti, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Subhūti!
It is well that you awaken these bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, to these points of attachment.
Therefore, Subhūti, I shall explain to you other attachments that are even more subtle."
Listen to them, and attend to them well and thoroughly;
I shall speak to you.
"Excellent, Blessed One," the venerable Subhūti replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this: "In this regard, Subhūti, a faithful son of good family or daughter of good family attends to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened one, by way of signs.
Now, Subhūti, as many as there are signs, so many are attachments."
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, attachment arises from signs.
Thus, I rejoice in those untainted dharmas of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present.

Having thus rejoiced, one dedicates the root of merit associated with that rejoicing toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, thinking, "I dedicate this. Furthermore, Subhūti, that which is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of phenomena is neither past, nor future, nor present.
That which is neither past, nor future, nor present is liberated from the three times;
that which is liberated from the three times—
It cannot be transformed, nor can it be made into a sign, nor can it be made into an object of focus;
nor is it seen, heard, thought, or cognized.
Subhūti said: "The intrinsic nature of phenomena, Blessed One, is profound.
The Blessed One said: "Because it is secluded, Subhūti.
Subhūti said: "The perfection of wisdom, Blessed One, is profound by its very nature."
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, because it is pure by nature,
because it is secluded by nature, the perfection of wisdom is profound by nature."
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is by nature secluded.
O Blessed One, I pay homage to the perfection of wisdom."
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, all dharmas are also by nature secluded.
And that which, Subhūti, is the natural seclusion of all dharmas, that is the perfection of wisdom."
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, all dharmas have been realized by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, as uncreated.
Subhūti said: "In that case, Blessed One, have all dharmas not been realized by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One?"
The Blessed One said: "For it is thus, Subhūti, that by their very nature those dharmas are nothing at all;
and that which is their nature is non-nature."
And that which is intrinsic nature—
that intrinsic nature is because all phenomena have a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.
Therefore, Subhūti, all phenomena were not fully awakened to by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, there are not two natures of phenomena;
for, Subhūti, there is only one single nature of all phenomena.
And that which, Subhūti, is the intrinsic nature of all phenomena,
that is a non-nature; and that which is a non-nature, [that is the intrinsic nature].
That is their intrinsic nature.
In this way, Subhūti, all these millions of attachments are avoided.
Subhūti said, "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is profound.
The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is profound because space is profound.
Subhūti said, "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to realize."
The Blessed One said: "For indeed, Subhūti, no one at all attains full awakening.
Subhūti said: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is inconceivable.
The Blessed One said: "For indeed, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is not to be known by the mind, nor is it to be traversed by the mind."
He said: "Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is uncreated.
The Blessed One replied: "Subhūti, because no agent is apprehended, the perfection of wisdom is uncreated."
He said: "In that case, Blessed One, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice in the perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One replied: "Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the perfection of wisdom, does not practice in form, he practices in the perfection of wisdom."
Thus, if one does not course in feeling, nor in perception, nor in mental formations;
if one does not course in consciousness,
then one courses in the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not course in the thought that "form is impermanent," one courses in the perfection of wisdom;
the same applies to feeling, perception, and mental formations.
If one does not course in the thought that "consciousness is impermanent," one courses in the perfection of wisdom;
if one does not course in the thought that "form is empty," [one courses in the perfection of wisdom].
He practices in the perfection of wisdom.
It is the same for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
If he does not practice with the thought that "consciousness is empty," [he practices in the perfection of wisdom].
He courses in the perfection of wisdom.
If he does not course [with the thought] that "form is incomplete" or "form is complete," he courses in the perfection of wisdom.
That which is the incompleteness or completeness of form is not that form;
the same applies to feeling, perception, and mental formations.
If one does not course in the notion that consciousness is incomplete or complete,
one courses in the perfection of wisdom.
And as for that which is the incompleteness or completeness of consciousness—
That is not consciousness.
If one does not even practice in this way,
one practices in the perfection of wisdom.

When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how far-reaching it is that the state of attachment and the state of non-attachment of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, have been thus explained.
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, when one does not course in the thought that 'form is with attachment' or 'without attachment,' one courses in the perfection of wisdom."
In the same way, Subhūti, when one does not course in the thought that feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness are with attachment or without attachment,
one courses in the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not course in the notion that "the eye is with attachment or without attachment," one courses in the perfection of wisdom.
Likewise, up to the point of feeling born of mind-contact, if one does not course in the notion that it is "with attachment or without attachment," [one courses in the perfection of wisdom].
One practices in the perfection of wisdom;
one does not practice in the perfection of wisdom by thinking that "the earth element is with attachment" or "without attachment.
One practices in the perfection of wisdom.

As long as one does not course in the notion that the element of consciousness is "with attachment" or "without attachment," one courses in the perfection of wisdom. One does not course in the notion that the perfection of generosity is "with attachment" or "without attachment."

He courses in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, he does not course in the thought that "the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom are with attachment or without attachment."
One practices in the perfection of wisdom.

Likewise, one does not practice with the thought that the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are "with attachment" or "without attachment";
thus one practices in the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice with the thought that the fruit of stream-entry is "with attachment" or "without attachment," one practices in the perfection of wisdom.

Likewise, if one does not practice with the thought that the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arhatship is "with attachment" or "without attachment," [one practices in the perfection of wisdom].
He courses in the perfection of wisdom;
he does not course with the thought that "the state of a Pratyekabuddha is with attachment or without attachment," for thus he courses in the perfection of wisdom.
If one does not practice with the thought that "Buddhahood is with attachment" or "without attachment," one practices in the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti, even regarding omniscience, if one does not practice with the thought that it is "with attachment" or "without attachment," [one practices in the perfection of wisdom].
He courses in the perfection of wisdom.
Coursing in this way, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not produce attachment to form, nor to feeling, nor to perception, nor to volitional formations.
He does not produce attachment to consciousness; he does not produce attachment to the eye, nor up to the feeling born of mind-contact, does he produce attachment.
He does not produce attachment to the earth element, nor does he produce attachment up to the consciousness element;
he does not produce attachment to the perfection of generosity.

He does not produce attachment to the perfection of ethical discipline, nor to the perfection of patience, nor to the perfection of vigor, nor to the perfection of meditative concentration, nor to the perfection of wisdom;
nor to the factors conducive to awakening, nor to the powers.
He does not produce attachment toward the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
He does not produce attachment to the fruit of stream-entry;
he does not produce attachment to the fruit of once-returning, nor to the fruit of non-returning, nor to arhatship;
he does not produce attachment to the state of a pratyekabuddha.
He does not produce attachment to Buddhahood, nor does he produce attachment to omniscience.
Why is that?
For, Subhūti, omniscience is indeed unattached, unbound, unliberated, and not transcended.
Thus, Subhūti, for the sake of transcending all attachments, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should practice the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti said: "It is wonderful, Blessed One! How profound, Blessed One, is this Dharma called the perfection of wisdom, which does not diminish even while it is being taught."
Even when not being taught, it does not diminish;
even when being taught, it does not increase;
and even when not being taught, it does not increase.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: "Excellent, excellent, Subhūti!
It is so, Subhūti, it is so.
For example, Subhūti, suppose a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha were to remain for the duration of his life speaking of the qualities of space."
There would be no increase of space;
even when a sound is not uttered, there would be no decrease of space.
Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, a person created by magic is neither attracted nor afflicted even when his praises are being spoken.
Even when sounds are not being uttered, it is neither obstructed nor afflicted;
in the very same way, Subhūti, that which is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of phenomena, [is likewise].
Whether it is being taught, it remains exactly that much; whether it is not being taught, it remains exactly that much.

The Elder Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, while coursing in the profound perfection of wisdom and cultivating the perfection of wisdom, neither desponds nor becomes elated, and yet applies himself to yoga in this very matter— he is a doer of what is difficult."
And he does not turn back.
O Blessed One, this cultivation of the perfection of wisdom is indeed the cultivation of space.
O Blessed One, those bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, are worthy of homage.
For what reason is this?
Blessed One, he who binds on the armor for the sake of sentient beings desires to bind it together with space itself.
“Blessed One, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who has donned the great armor.

Blessed One, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is a hero who desires to don the armor for the sake of beings who are equal to space and beings who are equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), desiring to awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Blessed One, he is one who desires to liberate space itself.”

“O Blessed One, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having donned the armor for the sake of beings who are equal to space and equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), dons that armor, O Blessed One, has attained the armor of the great perfection of vigor; he wishes to lift up space itself.
Then, a certain monk, bowing with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, said this to the Blessed One: “I pay homage, Blessed One, to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).”
For in this way, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom does not produce any dharma,
nor does it cause any dharma to cease.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Subhūti: "Noble Subhūti, if one here applies oneself to yoga in this very perfection of wisdom, where will he apply himself to yoga?
Subhūti replied: "Kauśika, he will apply himself to yoga in space."

Kauśika, whoever shall apply themselves to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom will apply themselves to the yoga in open space— whosoever thinks that they should train in the perfection of wisdom and apply themselves to its yoga.
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One command me;
I shall provide protection, defense, and guardianship for that son of good family or daughter of good family who upholds this perfection of wisdom.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to Śakra, lord of the gods: “Kauśika, do you perceive that dharma for which you would provide protection, defense, and guardianship?”
Śakra said: "Certainly not, Noble Subhūti.
Subhūti said: "In this way, Kauśika, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva shall abide in the perfection of wisdom as it has been explained, that itself will be his protection, defense, and guard."
Then, if he becomes separated from the perfection of wisdom,
humans and non-humans who look for a weak point and seek a weak point will find an opportunity to attack him.
Furthermore, Kauśika, one might as well think that protection, shelter, and defense should be arranged for space.
"Whoever should think that they must provide protection, defense, and guardianship for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom—
what do you think, Kauśika, are you able to provide protection, defense, and guardianship for an echo?
Śakra replied, "Certainly not, noble Subhūti."
Subhūti said: "In the same way, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing and dwelling in the perfection of wisdom thoroughly understands that all phenomena are like an echo;
and he does not conceive of them, nor does he perceive them."
He does not know, he does not perceive;
and he dwells with the thought that those phenomena do not exist, are not seen, are not found, and are not apprehended.
If he dwells in this way, [he is practicing rightly].
He courses in the perfection of wisdom.
Then, indeed, by the power of the Buddha, all the four great kings in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system,
all the Śakras, lords of the gods,
and all the Mahābrahmās—
And Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world—
these all approached the Blessed One;
having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood to one side.
And those great kings, all the Śakras, lords of the gods, all the gods of the Brahma-realm, and the Mahābrahmās, stood to one side.
And by the power of the Buddha, through the Buddha’s empowerment, Mahābrahmā Sahāpati caused a thousand Buddhas to attend to him;
by these very names, these very words, these very syllables, and by monks with the very name Subhūti, this very perfection of wisdom was taught, this very chapter on the perfection of wisdom.
There too, the Śakras themselves, the lords of the gods, questioned and inquired: "In this very spot on earth, this very Perfection of Wisdom was spoken;
and Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, will likewise speak this very Perfection of Wisdom in this very spot on earth."
The eighth chapter, titled "Purity," in the Noble Eight Thousand Line Perfection of Wisdom.
(Vaidya 100) Chapter Nine: The Chapter on Praise.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, 'perfection of wisdom' is merely a name."
And that name "this" is not apprehended;
it is said that a name is merely a linguistic convention.
That perfection of wisdom, too, does not exist and is not apprehended.
Just as the name is,
so too is the perfection of wisdom;
just as the perfection of wisdom is, so too is the name.
These two dharmas do not exist and are not apprehended.
For what reason, Blessed One, will the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
teach this Perfection of Wisdom in this very spot on earth, with these very names, these very words, and these very syllables?

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: "For in this way, Subhūti, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya will fully awaken to the fact that form is neither permanent nor impermanent, that form is neither bound nor liberated,
and that it is absolutely pure."
In this way, one does not perceive feeling, nor perception, nor mental formations;
nor does one perceive consciousness as permanent or impermanent,
nor consciousness as bound or liberated.
"He will fully awaken to it as 'absolutely pure.

For this reason, Subhūti, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he will, in these very names, with these very words and syllables, and in this very spot of earth, speak this very Perfection of Wisdom."
When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, is this perfection of wisdom indeed utterly pure?
The Blessed One replied: "Subhūti, it is utterly pure because of the purity of form. Likewise for feeling, perception, and mental formations."
Subhūti, through the purity of consciousness, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
Subhūti, through the purity of the non-arising, non-ceasing, non-defilement, and non-purification of form, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
It is the same for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure because consciousness is neither produced nor ceased, and is neither defiled nor purified;
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure because space is pure;
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is completely pure because form is unstained and ungraspable.
In the same way, Subhūti, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unstained and ungrasped, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure; Subhūti,
because it is unstained by the utterances and expressions that are like space or an echo, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.
Subhūti, because it is free from all staining and anointing by means of the non-staining nature of all phenomena, the perfection of wisdom is utterly pure.

When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, truly well-gained are the gains of those sons of good family and daughters of good family to whom this perfection of wisdom shall even come to the range of hearing,
let alone those who will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, set it forth, teach it, explain it, proclaim it, and study it."
They shall have no disease of the eye,
no disease of the ear, no disease of the nose, no disease of the tongue, and no disease of the body;
nor shall there be any dullness of mind.
They shall not meet their end through the failure to avoid dangers.
Furthermore, many thousands of deities will follow closely behind them.
On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, wherever that son of good family or daughter of good family—the Dharma-preacher—shall speak the Perfection of Wisdom, [there they will be present].
"In each of those cases, he will generate a much greater amount of merit.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: "So it is, Subhūti, so it is.
Subhūti, there will be many thousands of deities [who will follow] that son of good family or daughter of good family."
They will follow closely behind him,
and many thousands of deities will come there, all desiring to hear the Dharma;
and they will provide protection, shelter, and defense for that Dharma-preacher as he speaks this Perfection of Wisdom.
For what reason?
Subhūti, for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, the perfection of wisdom is the unsurpassed jewel.
For this reason also, Subhūti, a son of good family or a daughter of good family will generate much more merit on that account.

Moreover, Subhūti, there will indeed be many obstacles to this profound perfection of wisdom while it is being written down, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, set in motion, taught, explained, and studied.
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, great jewels have many adversaries;
and according to their excellence, they have even more formidable adversaries.
And this, Subhūti, is the unsurpassed great jewel for the world, namely the perfection of wisdom;
it has set out for the benefit and happiness of the world,
and it is present by way of the non-arising, non-ceasing, non-defilement, and indestructibility of all phenomena.
Moreover, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom does not adhere to any dharma, it is not defiled by any dharma,
and it does not grasp at any dharma.
For what reason?
Because, Subhūti, all those dharmas do not exist and are not apprehended.
Since they are not apprehended, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is unstained.
"Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom is unstained.
For, Subhūti, because form is unstained, this perfection of wisdom is unstained;
and so too are feeling, perception, and mental formations."
Subhūti, because consciousness is unstained, this perfection of wisdom is unstained.
Subhūti, if even in this way a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive [anything],
he courses in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom does not cause any dharma to enter, nor to settle, nor to manifest, nor to demonstrate, nor to bring forth, nor to lead away.
Then, indeed, many thousands of sons of gods in the sky made sounds of joy and shouts of exultation, and they waved their garments, saying, "Aha!
We behold this second turning of the wheel of Dharma in Jambudvīpa!
Then the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Elder Subhūti: "Subhūti, this is not a second turning of the wheel of Dharma, nor is it the turning of any dharma whatsoever."
or turning back—
such, Subhūti, is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows: "This is a great perfection, O Blessed One, for that bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses non-attachment toward all phenomena—
that one who desires to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, yet does not fully awaken to any phenomenon whatsoever."
And he will turn the wheel of Dharma,
yet he will not demonstrate any dharma whatsoever.
Why is that?
For there is no dharma whatsoever that is perceived, nor any dharma that is indicated;
nor will anyone set forth any dharma.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, all phenomena are absolutely unproduced;
nor will they cause any phenomenon whatsoever to cease.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, all phenomena are unproduced from the very beginning,
owing to the fact that all phenomena are by nature secluded.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: "So it is, Subhūti; so it is.
For indeed, Subhūti, emptiness neither proceeds nor ceases.
Nor, Subhūti, does the signless proceed or cease."
Nor, Subhūti, does the wishless proceed or cease.
This teaching, Subhūti, which is thus taught,
is the teaching of all dharmas.
It has not been taught by anyone,
nor heard by anyone, nor received by anyone.
It has not been realized by anyone, it is not being realized by anyone, nor will it be realized by anyone.
Furthermore, by this teaching of the Dharma, no one has attained final nirvana, nor will anyone attain it, nor does anyone attain it;
nor by this teaching of the Dharma has anyone been made worthy of offerings.
When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One: "This is a perfection of non-existence, Blessed One, based on the non-existence of space.
This is a perfection of the equality of the unequaled, Blessed One, based on the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.
This is a perfection of solitude, Blessed One, based on absolute emptiness."
“Blessed One, this is the perfection of the uncrushable, based on the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the trackless, based on the absence of name and the absence of body.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the lack of intrinsic nature, based on the absence of coming and the absence of going.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-speaking, because of the non-conceptualization of all phenomena.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of namelessness, because of the non-apprehension of the aggregates.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-going, because of the non-coming of all phenomena.”
“Blessed One, this is the perfection of the unassailable, because all phenomena are ungraspable.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the inexhaustible, because it is joined with inexhaustible phenomena.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-arising, because all phenomena are not produced.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the non-agent, because an agent is not to be apprehended.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the non-knower, because all phenomena are without self.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-transmigration, because there is no occurrence of death and rebirth.”

“Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-discipline, because of the non-apprehension of objects in the past, future, and present. Blessed One, this is the perfection of dream, echo, reflection, mirage, and illusion, because of the communication of non-arising.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-defilement, because of the absence of intrinsic nature in passion, hatred, and delusion.”
“O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of non-purification, based on the non-apprehensibility of a basis. O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of non-staining, based on the non-staining of space.
O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of non-proliferation, based on the transcendence of all mental engagement with phenomena.”
“Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-conceptualization, by virtue of its immovability.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-agitation, by virtue of the stability of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
Blessed One, this is the perfection of dispassion, by virtue of the non-falsity of all phenomena.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-arising, because of the non-conceptuality of all phenomena.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of peace, because of the non-apprehension of the signs of all phenomena.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of faultlessness, because of the perfection of qualities.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of being free from afflictions, based on the non-existence of conceptual construction.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of being devoid of sentient beings, based on the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the immeasurable, based on the fact that all phenomena neither arise nor do not arise.”
“Blessed One, this is the perfection that does not follow after the two extremes, by virtue of non-attachment to all phenomena.

Blessed One, this is the unadulterated perfection, by virtue of the non-differentiation of all phenomena. Blessed One, this is the perfection that is untouched, by virtue of having no longing for the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-conceptuality, based on the equality of conceptualization.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the immeasurable, based on the immeasurability of phenomena.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of non-attachment, based on the non-attachment of all phenomena.”
“O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of impermanence, based on the unconditioned nature of all phenomena.

O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of suffering, based on the nature of phenomena being equal to space. O Bhagavān, this is the perfection of emptiness, based on the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of selflessness, because of the non-attachment to all dharmas.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of signlessness, because of the non-arising of all dharmas.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of all emptiness, because of its being infinite and boundless.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the factors conducive to awakening, such as the applications of mindfulness, because they are non-apprehendable.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, because the three gateways to liberation are non-apprehendable.
O Blessed One, this is the perfection of the eight liberations, because they are non-apprehendable.”
“Blessed One, this is the perfection of the nine successive dwellings, by virtue of the non-apprehensibility of the first dhyāna and so forth.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the four truths, by virtue of the non-apprehensibility of suffering and so forth.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the ten perfections, by virtue of the non-apprehensibility of giving and so forth.”
“O Blessed One, this is the perfection of power, based on being uncrushable.

O Blessed One, this is the perfection of fearlessness, based on absolute lack of dejection. O Blessed One, this is the perfection of analytical knowledge, based on the state of being unattached and unimpeded regarding omniscience.”
“Blessed One, this is the perfection of the unique qualities of all Buddhas, because it transcends all calculation.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the suchness of the Tathāgata, because it is the non-falsity of all phenomena.
Blessed One, this is the perfection of the Self-Existent One, because it is the absence of intrinsic nature in all phenomena.”

“O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the knowledge of the omniscient one, because it consists in the thorough comprehension of all aspects of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.”
The ninth chapter, titled "Praise," in the Noble Eight Thousand Line Perfection of Wisdom.
(Vaidya 104) Chapter Ten: The Proclamation of the Qualities of Retention.

Then, it occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "Those sons of good family and daughters of good family must have performed services under previous Victors and have planted roots of merit under many Buddhas."
And they will be sustained by spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), those to whom even this Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) comes within the range of their hearing;
how much more so for those who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, propagate, teach, instruct, and explain this very profound Perfection of Wisdom in such a manner?

They will study it; having taken it up, retained it, recited it, mastered it, set it in motion, taught it, instructed it, pointed it out, and recited it, they will train for the sake of suchness and practice for the sake of suchness.
They will apply themselves to yoga for the sake of suchness;
they will not be endowed with merely inferior roots of merit.
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have attended upon many Buddhas.
Those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will have been questioned and interrogated by those sons of good family and daughters of good family regarding this very perfection of wisdom;
and they too have heard this from the presence of former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones,
just as those who shall hear this perfection of wisdom even now.
Having heard it, they will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, explain it, set it forth, and study it;
they will train for the sake of suchness and practice for the sake of suchness.
They will apply themselves to the practice for the sake of suchness.
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family should be known as having planted roots of merit under many Buddhas,
who, while this very profound perfection of wisdom is being spoken, taught, explained, pointed out, and recited, do not shrink back and do not become despondent.
They will not be despondent, they will not fall into despair, they will not turn their minds away, and they will not become disheartened.
They will not be afraid, they will not be terrified, and they will not fall into a state of terror.

Then, the venerable Śāriputra, having understood with his own mind this very reflection in the mind of Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, while this profound perfection of wisdom is being spoken, taught, and explained here, should have faith, conviction, and resolute belief [in it]..."
With a serene mind, having generated the thought of awakening, they will take up this perfection of wisdom, maintain it, recite it, master it,
propagate it, teach it, explain it, proclaim it, study it,
and train themselves in accordance with suchness.
He will practice for the sake of suchness;
he will apply himself to yoga for the sake of suchness;
he should be regarded as an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva.
For what reason?
Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is profound.

Indeed, Blessed One, one who possesses only meager roots of merit, who is not by nature inquisitive, and who has not previously practiced while in the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, would not [grasp] this very same profound [perfection of wisdom] here.
The perfection of wisdom can be resolved upon with faith.
However, those who, failing to resolve upon it and failing to understand it, think it should be rejected—
O Bhagavat, even in the past, these sons of good family and daughters of good family rejected this profound perfection of wisdom when it was being spoken.
For what reason?
Because their roots of merit are so limited.
Indeed, Blessed One, it is not possible for those who have not practiced in the past to have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, those who shall reject this profound *prajñāpāramitā* while it is being spoken should be known as follows: even in the past, when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* was being spoken, they rejected it.
For indeed, they lack faith when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being spoken.
They have no patience, no inclination, no desire, no vigor, no heedfulness, and no resolute faith;
nor have they previously questioned the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, or the disciples of the Buddhas regarding these matters.
And they have not been subjected to interrogation.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāriputra: "Noble Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom is profound.
What is there to be wondered at if a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not previously practiced would lack faith when this profound perfection of wisdom is being taught?
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "I pay homage, Blessed One, to the perfection of wisdom!"
“O Blessed One, he who pays homage to the perfection of wisdom pays homage to the knowledge of the All-Knowing One.
The Blessed One said, “It is even so, Kauśika; it is just as you have said.”
Kauśika, he who pays homage to the perfection of wisdom pays homage to the knowledge of the omniscient one.
Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, the omniscience of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, is born from this.
Furthermore, the perfection of wisdom is manifested as having arisen from the knowledge of the omniscient one.
Thus should one course in this perfection of wisdom;
thus should one abide in this perfection of wisdom.
In this way one should practice in this perfection of wisdom;
in this way one should apply oneself to yoga in this perfection of wisdom.

Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, abide in the perfection of wisdom; and how, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, does he apply himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "Excellent, excellent, Kauśika!"
Excellent indeed, Kauśika, that you consider it necessary to ask and to question the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, regarding this matter.
This inspired eloquence of yours, Kauśika, has arisen through the power of the Buddha.
Here, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not abide in form.
He does not abide in the thought, "This is form.
Because, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide in form, he does not abide in the thought, "This is form."
In this way, he applies himself to yoga;
likewise, he does not abide in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
He does not abide in "consciousness.
Because, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abide in consciousness,
nor does he abide in the notion that "this is consciousness."
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of consciousness.
O Kauśika, one does not apply [the mind] to "form";
because, O Kauśika, one does not apply [the mind] to "form," [one applies oneself to the yoga].
In this way, he does not abide in the thought "this is form";
likewise for feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness, O Kauśika, he does not apply himself to them.
Because, Kauśika, he does not apply the designation "consciousness," thus he does not abide in the notion of "consciousness.
In this way, he becomes one who stands in the perfection of wisdom.
In this way, one enters into yoga.
Then, indeed, the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: “Profound, O Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom;
difficult to fathom, O Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom;
difficult to grasp, O Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom.”
“Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
The Blessed One said, “So it is, Śāriputra; so it is.
Śāriputra, one does not abide in the notion that ‘form is profound.’”
For this reason, Śāriputra, when one does not abide in the notion that "form is profound," in this way one applies oneself to yoga with respect to form;
and likewise for feeling, perception, and mental formations.
Śāriputra, one does not abide in the thought that "consciousness is profound.
Śāriputra, because one does not abide in the thought that "consciousness is profound," in this way one applies oneself to yoga with respect to consciousness.
Śāriputra, one does not apply oneself to the thought that "form is deep.
Śāriputra, because one does not apply oneself to the thought that "form is deep," one likewise does not abide in the thought that "form is deep."

In the same way, Śāriputra, one does not apply oneself to the thought that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound. Because, Śāriputra, one does not apply oneself to the thought that consciousness is profound, [one does not apprehend it].
In this way, one does not abide in the notion that "consciousness is profound."

When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, the profound perfection of wisdom should be spoken in the presence of an irreversible, prophesied bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Why is that?"
For he, Blessed One, will not hesitate, will not doubt, will not be perplexed, and will not dispute.

Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāriputra: "Venerable Śāriputra, if this Perfection of Wisdom were spoken in the presence of an unprophesied bodhisattva mahāsattva, what fault would there be?"
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "Kauśika, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has come from afar.

Kauśika, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long since set out in the vehicle and has matured his roots of virtue, he who, though not yet predicted [to enlightenment], shall obtain this perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, worshipping, attending upon, and hearing it."
Having heard this, he will not be terrified, will not be frightened, and will not fall into fear;
it should be known that he will receive the prophecy of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment before long, for his prophecy is near at hand.
That bodhisattva mahāsattva will not bypass one, two, or three Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas;
from them, he will receive the prophecy regarding his unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Moreover, he will please them.
Having pleased those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, he will not cause them to be displeased;
and his vision of the Tathāgatas will not be in vain,
for through that vision of the Tathāgatas, he will thereafter obtain the prophecy of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

And until he receives the prophecy of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, he will not let the seeing, bowing to, attending upon, and serving of the Tathāgatas be in vain, until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, that bodhisattva mahāsattva must have come from afar;
he has long been set out upon the vehicle. For it should be known, Blessed One, that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is one whose roots of virtue are fully ripened."

Whoever shall obtain this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the purpose of seeing, worshipping, attending upon, and hearing it—how much more so then for one who, having heard it, shall take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct in it, explain it, and study it? Then the Blessed One said this to the venerable Śāriputra: "So it is, Śāriputra; so it is."
Śāriputra, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has come from afar;
he has long since set out in the vehicle.
For, Śāriputra, that bodhisattva mahāsattva will have fully ripened roots of merit.

Whoever shall obtain this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the purpose of seeing, saluting, attending upon, and hearing it—how much more so, then, he who, having heard it, shall take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, explain it, proclaim it, and study it? Then the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One: "It occurs to me, Blessed One..."
It occurs to me, O Sugata, that there is an illustrative analogy.
Just as if, Blessed One, a son of good family or a daughter of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle were to sit upon the seat of enlightenment even while in a dream—
it should be known, Blessed One, that this is so.
"This bodhisattva mahāsattva is close to the full awakening of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

In the same way, Blessed One, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall obtain this profound perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, venerating, attending upon, and hearing it, [he or she is likewise close to full awakening].
How much more so, Blessed One, regarding one who has heard it and is able to grasp it, retain it, recite it, master it, propagate it, teach it, instruct it, explain it, and study it!
It should be known, Blessed One, that this person belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle has come from afar and has long since set out in the vehicle;
this person belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle is close to receiving the prediction of enlightenment.

The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will prophesy that this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva shall attain the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Indeed, it should be known that this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has long since set out in the vehicle and has fully ripened his roots of merit,
for whom this profound perfection of wisdom will arise, even if only for the sake of hearing it.

How much more so, Blessed One, is this the case for a son of good family or a daughter of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, propagate, teach, explain, proclaim, and study this profound perfection of wisdom?
For what reason?
For the most part, Blessed One, sentient beings have been conditioned by accumulations of karma that lead to the ruin of the Dharma;
for the most part, their minds will be averse to this profound perfection of wisdom, and their minds will recoil from it.
For sentient beings who have not accumulated roots of merit do not, for the most part, enter into or find faith in this reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).

Rather, O Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family whose minds enter into and find faith in this reality-limit should be known as having indeed accumulated roots of merit, as having well-accumulated roots of merit.
